passage.title: Teacher-written extract for the Year 7 assessment point 2 test (TGA)
paras: Before six, the harbour belongs to the gulls. They patrol the quay like bored guards, shrieking at nothing. Then the boats come in, one by one, low in the water with the night's catch, and the quiet breaks open. Engines cough and die. Ropes are thrown, caught and tied in a single movement that the fishermen have made ten thousand times. My uncle is always the last to land. He climbs the ladder slowly, salt drying white on his sleeves, and before he says a word to anyone he looks back at the sea, the way you might look at a difficult friend.

keywords.def: a text you have not studied before
explain how and why a writer's choices create effects
working alone, in silence, within a set time

questions.q: Before the timer: underline the key word in question 1
questions.a: Question 1 asks 'Who does the harbour belong to before six?': key word 'before six'.

questions.q: Core (timed, 20 minutes): Section A. 1) Who does the harbour belong to before six? (1) 2) Give two sounds the boats make or cause. (2) 3) What does 'low in the water' suggest about the catch? (2) 4) How does the writer make the harbour come alive? Use PETZAAL. (8) 5) What does the last sentence suggest about the uncle's feelings for the sea? (3)
questions.a: 1) the gulls. 2) engines cough; engines die (or ropes thrown). 3) the boats are heavy, so the catch is large. 4) PETZAAL on, for example, the simile 'like bored guards', personification 'Engines cough and die', the contrast of quiet and noise. 5) respect mixed with wariness: he treats the sea as a 'difficult friend'.

questions.q: Extend (timed, 5 minutes): Section B. 6) Label the word classes in 'The old boat rocked gently.' (2) 7) Rewrite in the passive: 'The fishermen tied the ropes.' (2) 8) Add a colon to introduce a list: 'He carried three things a net, a knife and a flask.' (2)
questions.a: 6) The (determiner) old (adjective) boat (noun) rocked (verb) gently (adverb). 7) The ropes were tied by the fishermen. 8) He carried three things: a net, a knife and a flask.

questions.q: Stretch (timed, 8 minutes): Section C. Describe a busy place at dawn in one paragraph, using one metaphor and one personification.
questions.a: Marked for imagery (4) and accuracy of sentences and punctuation (4).

questions.q: Question 4 is worth 8 marks. What should your answer include?
options: a retelling of the whole text
a point, a quotation and an explanation of the writer's choice
questions.a: B) a point, a quotation and an explanation of the writer's choice. Eight marks rewards PETZAAL: point, evidence, technique, zoom and analysis.
